subject: Per-route snapshot instrumentation checklist + exception capture request
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-ops@acme.io
Date: Sun, 3 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Per-route snapshot instrumentation checklist + exception capture request

Hi team —

Quick background: Acme hit a tenant-induced cost spike last week that we only partially reconstructed from traces. They asked for a reproducible per-route snapshot (cost + tail latency) that ops can pull on-demand during an incident. They want the snapshot to capture: active route config, recent batching profile, KV cache hit ratio, token path distribution, and the last 1,000 tokens + timestamps for any long-running request.

As part of the Console observability work, can we define a small, implementation-ready instrumentation checklist and an exception-capture flow so we can hand this to Acme as a supported artifact? Specifically I’m asking for: 
- A concrete list of metrics/events we must include in the snapshot (names + units).
- Minimal retention window and sampling rules (how to avoid huge exports).
- A simple API or Console button idea for ops to trigger and download the snapshot.
- UX/permissions notes (who can run snapshots; audit log entries).
- A fallback capture when a route is using an older model variant.

I attached a draft schema (sample-snapshot-schema.yaml) and a small excerpt of the spike logs. Can we turn this into an actionable checklist that the observability team can implement in the next sprint?

Proposed next step: 30m sync tomorrow 10:30am PT to walk the checklist and agree on owners. If that time doesn’t work, propose alternatives.

Thanks —
Logan
Logan Wright
Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-ops@acme.io
Date: Sun, 3 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Per-route snapshot instrumentation checklist + exception capture request

Thanks Logan — good framing. A few clarifying questions before the sync: 

1) For "token path distribution" do you mean per-token model ops counts (e.g., attention steps) or the higher-level token class histogram (prompt vs. completion vs. toolcall)? I suspect the latter is easier but wanted to confirm.

2) For the "last 1,000 tokens + timestamps" — do you want the full text payload (redacted PII) or just token IDs/timings? Customers often ask for full payloads which triggers our privacy review.

3) Sampling rules: is the ask to always cap exports to a single request bundle (e.g., 1,000 tokens) OR to allow a rolling window that can span multiple requests? The rolling window is more useful for correlated spikes but heavier.

I sketched a minimal metric set in the attached schema but can tighten it up: 
- route_id (string)
- route_config_hash (hex)
- active_model_variant (string)
- avg_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99)
- tokens_generated (count)
- batching_depth (histogram)
- kv_cache_hit_rate (fraction)
- long_request_snapshot: {token_ids, token_timestamps, redaction_flags}

For the sync: 10:30am PT works for me. I’ll bring a short demo of existing trace exports and a draft API surface.

— Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Eng, Observability
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-ops@acme.io
Date: Sun, 3 Jun 2028 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Per-route snapshot instrumentation checklist + exception capture request

Looping in implementation constraints from infra/ops perspective: 

- Size: snap exports must be bounded. We should enforce a hard cap (tarball <= 25MB) and prefer structured jsonl with compressed chunks. The 1,000-token request payload (IDs + timestamps) should be optional by default and require an "include-long-requests" flag that is gated by a role.
- Performance: snapshot generation must be backgrounded; synchronous capture during a P95 incident will add latency if not carefully isolated. Recommend: a capture job that reads from replicated in-memory cache and KV snapshots, not the live serving path.
- Backward variants: when a route is using older model variants without precise KV metrics, snapshot should emit a compatibility note and best-effort placeholders.

Attachments: I exported a truncated tenant trace (tenant-spike-log.txt) to show the typical size and the places we’d need cross-service joins.

I can take ownership of the capture job prototype if we agree on an interface by EOW (end of week).

Ben
Ben Carter
SRE / Observability
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-ops@acme.io, marie.tran@acme.com
Date: Sun, 3 Jun 2028 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Per-route snapshot instrumentation checklist + exception capture request

Thanks everyone. Quick notes from product/roadmap perspective: 

- Scope: this should be a small, well-defined capability worth shipping as an "incident snapshot" MVP rather than full export orchestration. MVP scope: metric bundle + route metadata + optional long-request bundle (role-gated).
- Owners: Jasmine — schema & Console UI surface; Ben — capture job prototype and service-level joins; Logan — acceptance criteria + customer communication; I’ll own the prioritization and roadmap slotting.
- Timeline: propose we land an API spec + checklist by Thu 6/6, prototype capture job by Tue 6/11, and a customer-facing demo for Acme w/c 6/17. If any timeline looks off please flag now.

Action items: 
1) Jasmine: post final schema to the Drive link and update OBS-5421 by EOD Wed.
2) Ben: prototype a background worker that can assemble the bundle; include size cap and a compression option.
3) Logan: draft a short customer-facing one-pager that outlines what we will and will not include in the snapshot (for legal/privacy).

Agree to the 10:30am sync. I’ll share an invite.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product — Console
Redwood Inference
